clue.text: Cuts into two parts, taking half second

definitions.text: Cuts into two parts, taking half second

parts.words: Cuts into two parts, taking half second
parts.note: the plain sense is dividing something in two; the tail is a playful example, since splitting a second down the middle leaves each piece half a second long

explanation.surface: Someone slicing things in two, apparently in a hurry: half a second per cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening words do the defining; 'taking half second' adds a whimsical instance of halving rather than separate wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide into two equal portions is exactly the geometric sense of the verb, here in its third-person form.

clue.text: Little girl with fish to sell down the river

parts.note: Bet is a short form of the girl's name Betty or Elizabeth
a ray is a flat cartilaginous fish such as a skate

explanation.surface: A small girl taking a fish off to market downriver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sell down the river' is an idiom for being treacherous, not trading on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone down the river is an idiom for treacherously abandoning or double-crossing them.

clue.text: Drink that is mixed and cast around

indicators.note: the word for cast is placed around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to shy is to fling or throw, as at a coconut shy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for a cocktail: mix it, then throw it about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like part of the bartending; it means throw (SHY), which goes 'around' AND.
explanation.definitionFit: This drink is a blend of beer with lemonade or ginger beer, so it is literally a mixed one.

clue.text: Changed circumstances may put a different complexion on them

definitions.text: Changed circumstances may put a different complexion on them

parts.words: Changed circumstances may put a different complexion on them
parts.note: the idiom about a situation looking different is taken literally: certain lizards alter their skin colour to match new surroundings

explanation.surface: A remark about how new circumstances can change how people see things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put a different complexion on' is usually figurative; here it means a literal change of skin colour.
explanation.definitionFit: These lizards are famous for shifting skin colour according to their surroundings, so new settings literally recolour them.

clue.text: Checks foundation garments

definitions.meaning: halts or postpones, as in a judge halting an execution
corsets stiffened with bone, once worn as underwear

explanation.walkthrough: 'Foundation garments' is a period term for corsetry; old corsets were called by this plural name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a judge halts proceedings with such orders, and corsets were traditionally known by this word.

clue.text: Bill is an aristocrat, it's said

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken, so we want a word with the same sound

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman, so 'an aristocrat' gives A COUNT

explanation.surface: Bill turns out to be a nobleman, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is the invoice sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill and this word both mean a statement of money owed, as in a shop or restaurant tab.

clue.text: Sadly Pat and Ernest split up for now

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of the names that follow are disturbed
the couple's breakup doubles as the instruction to break the letters of the names and reassemble them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple, Pat and Ernest, have parted ways, at least for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean currently or for the time being, as in 'that's all we know so far'.

clue.text: Signals and strikes the ball?

definitions.meaning: prompts given to actors telling them when to speak or enter
in snooker or billiards a player hits the ball with a long stick; the question mark flags that the stick's name is used as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the snooker one: to play a stroke with the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both prompts to performers and, in billiards, playing a shot with the stick.

clue.text: Tune died out, in need of revising

indicators.note: out here means wrong or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A melody faded away and now needs reworking.
explanation.definitionFit: Text not yet checked or corrected by an editor still needs revising.

clue.text: Insisted on getting amended order

indicators.note: amended means altered or corrected, so the letters of the first word are changed round

explanation.surface: Someone demanded that an order be revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command; it means neatness. 'On getting' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatness and good order are synonyms: a tidy room is an orderly one.

clue.text: A temple ornament?

parts.note: temple suggests a place of worship, but it is the side of the head, where a jewelled band sits

explanation.surface: Seemingly a decoration in a religious building.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'temple' is the side of the forehead, not a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled semicircular headpiece rests at the temples, so it is literally a head ornament.

clue.text: Fear capture

definitions.meaning: to dread or anticipate with anxiety, an older sense
to arrest or seize, as police do a suspect

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to anticipate with dread and to seize a suspect, as in police arrests.

clue.text: Letter-openers?

parts.note: not paper knives but the people who open mail because it was sent to them

explanation.surface: Seemingly a desk tool for slitting envelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the openers are people, the recipients, not knives.
explanation.definitionFit: Recipients of letters are the ones entitled to open them.

clue.text: Beast left one with no going back

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: going back says the little word 'no' is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: An animal left on its own with no way to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no going back' sounds like irrevocability; 'going back' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat is the classic king of beasts.

clue.text: Having surveyed houses one may warn of future problems

definitions.text: Having surveyed houses one may warn of future problems

parts.words: Having surveyed houses one may warn of future problems
parts.note: sounds like a building surveyor, but the houses are the twelve divisions of a horoscope chart, read to predict the future

explanation.surface: A building surveyor flagging structural trouble ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: In horoscopes the sky is divided into twelve 'houses', which a stargazer examines before forecasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Horoscope readers study the twelve houses of the zodiac chart to forecast events.

clue.text: It's not in one's own interest to display it

definitions.text: It's not in one's own interest to display it

parts.words: It's not in one's own interest to display it
parts.note: the quality of acting for others rather than oneself is, by definition, against one's own interest

explanation.surface: Advice that showing some trait would harm you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in one's own interest' sounds like a warning, but it is a literal description of altruism.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism means putting others first, so showing it does not serve oneself.

clue.text: The last people you expect to see in knockout competitions

definitions.text: The last people you expect to see in knockout competitions

parts.words: The last people you expect to see in knockout competitions
parts.note: 'last people you expect' usually means unlikely; here it means those appearing in the final round

explanation.surface: Seemingly unlikely entrants turning up at a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'last people you'd expect' is read literally: the last ones left in a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitors who reach the deciding match are the last remaining in an elimination tournament.

clue.text: Two fools in killer combination

parts.note: an ass is a fool, and two of them give the word twice
the second of the pair of fools
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair of idiots working together as a murderous team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combination' just links the pieces placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired murderer, especially of a public figure, is a killer.

clue.text: One that's learned what's not practical

definitions.meaning: a scholar or university teacher, a learned person
purely theoretical, as in 'the question is purely theoretical'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' is the adjective (scholarly), not the past tense of learn.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a university scholar and also means theoretical rather than of practical relevance.

clue.text: Mistakenly denounces art that's now done without thinking

indicators.note: mistakenly says the letters are put down wrongly and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic wrongly condemning art that has become routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's now' is link; the definition is an adjectival phrase for a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit so ingrained that it happens automatically, without conscious thought, is the fixed phrase.

clue.text: Old guards about to get settled

indicators.note: guards means surrounds protectively, so the word for old encloses the other piece

parts.note: aged means old
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: Elderly sentries about to reach a settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old guards' looks like a veteran group; 'guards' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter that is settled has been decided by both parties, i.e. consented to.

clue.text: Attitude that a driver may take on a course

definitions.meaning: a position or point of view on an issue

definitions.text: that a driver may take on a course
definitions.meaning: a golfer with a driver club adopts a position of the feet before hitting on the golf course

explanation.walkthrough: The 'driver' is a golf club user, not a motorist, and the course is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an opinion held and the way a golfer positions their feet to hit.

clue.text: Articulates further and sums up

definitions.meaning: says something more, as in 'he went on to say'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sums up' looks like summarising; it is literal arithmetic totting up.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to say something more and to total numbers.

clue.text: Torch leaving burnt residue in passage

indicators.note: in says the residue sits inside the word for passage

parts.note: a flight is a passage through the air, or a flight of stairs
ash is what remains after burning
L stands for left, the past of leave, as on a departures board

explanation.surface: A torch burning down and leaving ash in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torch' suggests a flaming brand; it is the battery lamp. 'Leaving' supplies L (left), which follows ASH inside FLIGHT; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a torch is the battery-powered hand lamp Americans call by this name.

clue.text: A shade sanctimonious in the main

indicators.note: in places the word for sanctimonious within the sea

parts.note: the main is an old poetic term for the open sea
pi is informal shorthand for pious, sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A rather self-righteous figure, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'mostly', but 'the main' is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This reddish-brown colour, named after cuttlefish ink, is a shade.

clue.text: Manage to get note supporting policeman

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so the note comes after the policeman

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone getting by with a note backing up a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle a difficult situation successfully means to manage, as in 'she couldn't handle it'.

clue.text: Musters to call for drink

parts.note: to summon is to call for someone to come
to sup is to drink in sips

explanation.surface: Someone gathering courage before calling for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To muster courage and to gather it up are the same idiom, as in mustering strength.

clue.text: Gather information, alternating with the French

indicators.note: alternating with says the two pieces' letters are interleaved, one from each in turn

parts.note: gen is British slang for information; its letters G, E and N take turns
la is the French feminine for 'the'; its letters L and A sit between
the middle letter of gen, slang for information
the second letter of la, French for 'the'
the last letter of gen, slang for information

explanation.surface: Collecting details by switching between sources, including French ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather information' looks like the whole definition, but 'information' is GEN, whose letters alternate with LA.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather means to collect bit by bit, as when picking up leftover grain after harvest.

clue.text: Uncle out to get us — that's the heart of the matter

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of the relative's title are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A relative going out to fetch us, getting to the core of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' rearranges UNCLE into NUCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The central core of anything, like an atom's centre, is its heart.

clue.text: A game cut short

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A game ended early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' looks like it applies to the game; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text or book by cutting parts is the meaning, as in a condensed edition.
